title: Baba Dayal Das
definition: Baba Dayal Das (1783–1855) was a 19th-century Sikh reformer and the founder of the Nirankari movement, which sought to purge Sikhism of Brahmanical rituals and restore it to its original, formless (Nirankar) monotheistic roots.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the socio-religious reform movements in 19th-century Punjab, the evolution of Sikh identity, and the reaction against colonial-era religious syncretism.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Baba Dayal Das.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Socio-Religious Reform Movements of the 19th Century
Evolution of Sikhism (Guru Nanak to Guru Gobind Singh)
